passages.text: After Saul had returned from pursuing the Philistines, he was told, “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.”
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul had just finished chasing the Philistines.
People came to Saul.
They spoke to Saul.
They said, “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כַּֽאֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁ֣ב שָׁא֔וּל מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֣ה דָוִ֔ד בְּמִדְבַּ֖ר עֵ֥ין גֶּֽדִי׃ס

passages.text: So Saul took three thousand chosen men from all Israel and went to look for David and his men in the region of the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul chose three thousand men.
He chose the best men from all Israel.
Saul took these men with him.
Saul went to search for David.
David had men with him.
Saul looked for David and his men.
They searched in the region called the Rocks of the Wild Goats.
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֣ח שָׁא֗וּל שְׁלֹ֧שֶׁת אֲלָפִ֛ים אִ֥ישׁ בָּח֖וּר מִכָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ לְבַקֵּ֤שׁ אֶת־ דָּוִד֙ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֔יו עַל־ פְּנֵ֖י צוּרֵ֥י הַיְּעֵלִֽים׃

passages.text: Soon Saul came to the sheepfolds along the road, where there was a cave, and he went in to relieve himself. And David and his men were hiding in the recesses of the cave.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul traveled along the road.
He came to the sheepfolds.
There was a cave at that place.
Saul entered the cave to relieve himself.
David was not alone.
David and his men were inside the cave.
They were hiding in the back part of the cave.
passages.original: וַ֠יָּבֹא אֶל־ גִּדְר֨וֹת הַצֹּ֤אן עַל־ הַדֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ וְשָׁ֣ם מְעָרָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֥א שָׁא֖וּל לְהָסֵ֣ךְ אֶת־ רַגְלָ֑יו וְדָוִד֙ וַאֲנָשָׁ֔יו בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֥י הַמְּעָרָ֖ה יֹשְׁבִֽים׃

passages.text: So David’s men said to him, “This is the day about which the LORD said to you, ‘Behold, I will deliver your enemy into your hand, that you may do with him as you wish.’ ” Then David crept up secretly and cut off a corner of Saul’s robe.
passages.sermon:
David was hiding in a cave with his men.
Saul was their enemy.
David’s men spoke to him.
They said, “Today is the day the LORD spoke about to you.”
They said, “The LORD said, ‘I will give your enemy into your hand.’”
They said, “You may do to him whatever you think is good.”
David got up quietly.
David went to Saul without being seen.
David cut off a corner of Saul’s robe in secret.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמְרוּ֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י דָוִ֜ד אֵלָ֗יו הִנֵּ֨ה הַיּ֜וֹם אֲ‍ֽשֶׁר־ אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֣ה אֵלֶ֗יךָ הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י נֹתֵ֤ן אֶת־ אֹיְבֶיךָ בְּיָדֶ֔ךָ וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר יִטַ֣ב בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֗ד וַיִּכְרֹ֛ת אֶת־ כְּנַֽף־ הַמְּעִ֥יל אֲשֶׁר־ לְשָׁא֖וּל בַּלָּֽט׃

passages.text: Afterward, David’s conscience was stricken because he had cut off the corner of Saul’s robe.
passages.sermon:
David was a man chosen by God.
David hid in a cave with his men.
Saul, the king, entered the cave.
David secretly cut off a corner of Saul’s robe.
After this, David felt troubled in his heart.
David’s conscience hurt him.
He felt this way because he had cut the corner of Saul’s robe.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי֙ אַֽחֲרֵי־ כֵ֔ן וַיַּ֥ךְ לֵב־ דָּוִ֖ד אֹת֑וֹ עַ֚ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרַ֔ת אֶת־ כָּנָ֖ף אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְשָׁאֽוּל׃ס

passages.text: So he said to his men, “The LORD forbid that I should do such a thing to my master, the LORD’s anointed. May I never lift my hand against him, since he is the LORD’s anointed.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to his men.
David said, “The LORD forbids me to do this thing to my master.
My master is the LORD’s anointed.
I must not raise my hand against him.
He is the LORD’s anointed.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לַאֲנָשָׁ֜יו חָלִ֧ילָה לִּ֣י מֵֽיהוָ֗ה אִם־ אֶעֱשֶׂה֩ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֨ר הַזֶּ֤ה לַֽאדֹנִי֙ לִמְשִׁ֣יחַ יְהוָ֔ה לִשְׁלֹ֥חַ יָדִ֖י בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־ מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃

passages.text: With these words David restrained his men, and he did not let them rise up against Saul. Then Saul left the cave and went on his way.
passages.sermon:
David was a servant of God.
David had men with him in the cave.
David spoke to his men.
David used his words to stop his men.
David did not let his men attack Saul.
Saul was in the cave.
Saul got up and left the cave.
Saul went on his way.
passages.original: וַיְשַׁסַּ֨ע דָּוִ֤ד אֶת־ אֲנָשָׁיו֙ בַּדְּבָרִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א נְתָנָ֖ם לָק֣וּם אֶל־ שָׁא֑וּל וְשָׁא֛וּל קָ֥ם מֵהַמְּעָרָ֖ה וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃ס

passages.text: After that, David got up, went out of the cave, and called out to Saul, “My lord the king!” When Saul looked behind him, David bowed facedown in reverence and said to Saul, “Why do you listen to the words of men who say, ‘Look, David intends to harm you’?
passages.sermon:
David was a servant of God.
David respected King Saul.
After these things happened, David stood up.
David left the cave.
David called out to Saul.
David said, “My lord the king!”
Saul looked behind him.
David bowed down with his face to the ground.
David showed honor to Saul.
David spoke to Saul.
David said, “Why do you listen to men who say, ‘Look, David wants to harm you’?”
passages.original: וַיָּ֨קָם דָּוִ֜ד אַחֲרֵי־ כֵ֗ן וַיֵּצֵא֙ מִן־ הַמְּעָרָה וַיִּקְרָ֧א אַֽחֲרֵי־ שָׁא֛וּל לֵאמֹ֖ר אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיַּבֵּ֤ט שָׁאוּל֙ אַֽחֲרָ֔יו וַיִּקֹּ֨ד דָּוִ֥ד אַפַּ֛יִם אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃ס וַיֹּ֤אמֶר דָּוִד֙ לְשָׁא֔וּל לָ֧מָּה תִשְׁמַ֛ע אֶת־ דִּבְרֵ֥י אָדָ֖ם לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֣ה דָוִ֔ד מְבַקֵּ֖שׁ רָעָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Behold, this day you have seen with your own eyes that the LORD delivered you into my hand in the cave. I was told to kill you, but I spared you and said, ‘I will not lift my hand against my lord, since he is the LORD’s anointed.’
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Saul.
David said, “Today you saw something with your own eyes.
The LORD gave you into my hand in the cave.
Someone told me to kill you.
But I showed you mercy.
I said, ‘I will not raise my hand against my lord.’
You are the LORD’s anointed.”
passages.original: הִנֵּה֩ הַיּ֨וֹם הַזֶּ֜ה רָא֣וּ עֵינֶ֗יךָ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־ נְתָנְךָ֩ יְהוָ֨ה׀ הַיּ֤וֹם׀ בְּיָדִי֙ בַּמְּעָרָ֔ה וְאָמַ֥ר לַהֲרָגֲךָ֖ וַתָּ֣חָס עָלֶ֑יךָ וָאֹמַ֗ר לֹא־ אֶשְׁלַ֤ח יָדִי֙ בַּֽאדֹנִ֔י כִּי־ מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃

passages.text: See, my father, look at the corner of your robe in my hand. For I cut it off, but I did not kill you. See and know that there is no evil or rebellion in my hands. I have not sinned against you, even though you are hunting me down to take my life.
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Saul.
David called Saul "my father."
David told Saul to look at the corner of Saul’s robe.
David held the corner of Saul’s robe in his hand.
David said, “I cut off the corner of your robe.”
David said, “I did not kill you.”
David told Saul to see and know the truth.
David said, “There is no evil in my hand.”
David said, “There is no rebellion in my hand.”
David said, “I have not sinned against you.”
David said, “You are hunting me.”
David said, “You want to take my life.”
passages.original: וְאָבִ֣י רְאֵ֔ה גַּ֗ם רְאֵ֛ה אֶת־ כְּנַ֥ף מְעִילְךָ֖ בְּיָדִ֑י כִּ֡י בְּכָרְתִי֩ אֶת־ כְּנַ֨ף מְעִֽילְךָ֜ וְלֹ֣א הֲרַגְתִּ֗יךָ דַּ֤ע וּרְאֵה֙ כִּי֩ אֵ֨ין בְּיָדִ֜י רָעָ֤ה וָפֶ֙שַׁע֙ וְלֹא־ חָטָ֣אתִי לָ֔ךְ וְאַתָּ֛ה צֹדֶ֥ה אֶת־ נַפְשִׁ֖י לְקַחְתָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: May the LORD judge between you and me, and may the LORD take vengeance on you, but my hand will never be against you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the judge between you and me.
The LORD will decide who is right.
The LORD will take vengeance on you.
I will not harm you.
My hand will never be against you.
passages.original: יִשְׁפֹּ֤ט יְהוָה֙ בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֔ךָ וּנְקָמַ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה מִמֶּ֑ךָּ וְיָדִ֖י לֹ֥א תִֽהְיֶה־ בָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: As the old proverb says, ‘Wickedness proceeds from the wicked.’ But my hand will never be against you.
passages.sermon:
The old proverb says this.
Wicked people do wicked things.
I am not wicked.
I will not harm you.
My hand will never be against you.
passages.original: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יֹאמַ֗ר מְשַׁל֙ הַקַּדְמֹנִ֔י מֵרְשָׁעִ֖ים יֵ֣צֵא רֶ֑שַׁע וְיָדִ֖י לֹ֥א תִֽהְיֶה־ בָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Against whom has the king of Israel come out? Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog? A flea?
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Saul.
David was a young man.
Saul was the king of Israel.
David asked Saul a question.
David said, “Who have you come out against?”
David said, “Who are you chasing?”
David said, “Are you chasing a dead dog?”
David said, “Are you chasing a single flea?”
passages.original: אַחֲרֵ֨י מִ֤י יָצָא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַחֲרֵ֥י מִ֖י אַתָּ֣ה רֹדֵ֑ף אַֽחֲרֵי֙ כֶּ֣לֶב מֵ֔ת אַחֲרֵ֖י פַּרְעֹ֥שׁ אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: May the LORD be our judge and decide between you and me. May He take notice and plead my case and deliver me from your hand.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is our judge.
The LORD will decide between you and me.
The LORD will see what has happened.
The LORD will defend my cause.
The LORD will rescue me from your hand.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְדַיָּ֔ן וְשָׁפַ֖ט בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ וְיֵ֙רֶא֙ וְיָרֵ֣ב אֶת־ רִיבִ֔י וְיִשְׁפְּטֵ֖נִי מִיָּדֶֽךָ׃פ

passages.text: When David had finished saying these things, Saul called back, “Is that your voice, David my son?” Then Saul wept aloud and said to David, “You are more righteous than I, for you have rewarded me with good, though I have rewarded you with evil.
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Saul.
David finished saying these words to Saul.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul called out to David.
Saul said, “Is that your voice, my son David?”
Saul recognized David’s voice.
Saul raised his voice and wept.
Saul spoke to David.
Saul said, “You are more righteous than I am.”
Saul said, “You have done good to me.”
Saul said, “I have done evil to you.”
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י׀ כְּכַלּ֣וֹת דָּוִ֗ד לְדַבֵּ֞ר אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֤ים הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ אֶל־ שָׁא֔וּל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל הֲקֹלְךָ֥ זֶ֖ה בְּנִ֣י דָוִ֑ד וַיִּשָּׂ֥א שָׁא֛וּל קֹל֖וֹ וַיֵּֽבְךְּ׃ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ אֶל־ דָּוִ֔ד צַדִּ֥יק אַתָּ֖ה מִמֶּ֑נִּי כִּ֤י אַתָּה֙ גְּמַלְתַּ֣נִי הַטּוֹבָ֔ה וַאֲנִ֖י גְּמַלְתִּ֥יךָ הָרָעָֽה׃

passages.text: And you have shown this day how well you have dealt with me; for when the LORD delivered me into your hand, you did not kill me.
passages.sermon:
David acted kindly toward Saul today.
David showed Saul goodness.
The LORD gave Saul into David’s hand.
David did not kill Saul.
passages.original: וְאַתְּ הִגַּ֣דְתָּ הַיּ֔וֹם אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשִׂ֥יתָה אִתִּ֖י טוֹבָ֑ה אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר סִגְּרַ֧נִי יְהוָ֛ה בְּיָדְךָ֖ וְלֹ֥א הֲרַגְתָּֽנִי׃

passages.text: When a man finds his enemy, does he let him go away unharmed? May the LORD reward you with good for what you have done for me this day.
passages.sermon:
A man may find his enemy.
He can choose to let his enemy go free.
He can send his enemy away in peace.
This is not what most people do.
You did this for me today.
You let me go unharmed.
May the LORD give you good in return.
May the LORD reward you for your kindness to me today.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יִמְצָ֥א אִישׁ֙ אֶת־ אֹ֣יְב֔וֹ וְשִׁלְּח֖וֹ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ טוֹבָ֑ה וַֽיהוָה֙ יְשַׁלֶּמְךָ֣ טוֹבָ֔ה תַּ֚חַת הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשִׂ֖יתָה לִֽי׃

passages.text: Now I know for sure that you will be king, and that the kingdom of Israel will be established in your hands.
passages.sermon:
Saul spoke to David.
Saul was the king of Israel.
Saul said he now understood something clearly.
Saul said, “Now I know for sure you will be king.”
Saul said, “The kingdom of Israel will be established in your hands.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ הִנֵּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י מָלֹ֖ךְ תִּמְל֑וֹךְ וְקָ֙מָה֙ בְּיָ֣דְךָ֔ מַמְלֶ֖כֶת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So now, swear to me by the LORD that you will not cut off my descendants or wipe out my name from my father’s house.”
passages.sermon:
Saul spoke to David.
Saul asked David to make a promise.
Saul said, “Swear to me by the LORD.”
Saul asked David not to destroy his descendants after him.
Saul asked David not to wipe out his name from his father’s house.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה הִשָּׁ֤בְעָה לִּי֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה אִם־ תַּכְרִ֥ית אֶת־ זַרְעִ֖י אַֽחֲרָ֑י וְאִם־ תַּשְׁמִ֥יד אֶת־ שְׁמִ֖י מִבֵּ֥ית אָבִֽי׃

passages.text: So David gave his oath to Saul. Then Saul returned home, but David and his men went up to the stronghold.
passages.sermon: David swore an oath to Saul.\r\nSaul went to his house.\r\nDavid and his men went up to the stronghold.
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׁבַ֥ע דָּוִ֖ד לְשָׁא֑וּל וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ שָׁאוּל֙ אֶל־ בֵּית֔וֹ וְדָוִד֙ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֔יו עָל֖וּ עַל־ הַמְּצוּדָֽה׃פ
